press.oneLiner: Drivest is a UK-first navigation app built for learners and new drivers. Covering around 340 test centres and around 3000 structured practice routes across the UK.

tabs.title: Theory
tabs.line2: Build your foundation before you drive.

tabs.title: Practice
tabs.line1: Practice routes that start and end at your chosen test centre.
tabs.line2: Off-route alerts if you drift away from the route.

tabs.title: Navigation
tabs.line2: Choose lower-stress routes when alternatives exist.

why.title: Driving changes in stages. Drivest follows your stage.
bullets: After theory pass: you need structure.
Before test day: you need repetition.
After you pass: you need calm guidance.

coreUsps.title: UK-wide coverage
coreUsps.text: Coverage includes around 340 driving test centres and around 3000 structured practice routes across the UK.

coreUsps.title: Practice routes by centre
coreUsps.text: Pick a test centre. Choose a practice route. Start and finish at the same centre.

coreUsps.title: Off-route detection
coreUsps.text: If you move more than 50 metres away for 5 seconds, Drivest marks you off-route. It clears when you return.

coreUsps.title: Road feature prompts
coreUsps.text: Prompts for common features like roundabouts, traffic signals, zebra crossings, and school zones, based on map data and confidence rules.

coreUsps.title: Low-stress routing
coreUsps.text: When multiple routes exist, Drivest can prefer the lowest-stress option for lower confidence drivers.

coreUsps.title: Confidence score
coreUsps.text: Your confidence score adapts from your drives. It helps Drivest tune prompts and route choice.

coreUsps.title: Offline support
coreUsps.text: Download route and hazard packs. Keep core practice running when signal is weak.

steps.title: Choose your mode
steps.text: Learner, New Driver, or Standard. You can switch anytime.

steps.title: Pick a centre or destination
steps.text: Practice starts from a test centre. Navigation starts from your current location.

steps.title: Drive with calm prompts
steps.text: You see a prompt banner. You can enable voice, alerts only, or mute.

steps.title: Review your drive
steps.text: See stress and difficulty. Track progress over time.

pricing.title: Simple pricing. Clear access.

safety.title: Safety first
bullets: Drivest provides advisory prompts. It does not replace road signs.
Do not interact with the app while driving.
Follow the Highway Code and local rules.
arrivalAdvisory: Parking restrictions likely in this area.
Check local signage before leaving vehicle.

faq.a: No. Drivest is an independent app.
No. Drivest supports practice and awareness. Your driving decisions remain your responsibility.

faq.q: What makes Drivest different from Google Maps or Waze?
faq.a: Drivest focuses on learner and new driver needs. It adds practice routes, off-route alerts, stress scoring, confidence tuning, and a prompt system designed for early-stage drivers.
Map data and route packs. Prompt visibility depends on confidence rules.
Yes. You can choose Voice All, Alerts only, or Mute.
You can download route and hazard packs for areas you practise.
Prompts are brief. You control voice settings. Keep your attention on the road.

faq.q: Do you store my precise location?
faq.a: The app uses location for navigation. Analytics is optional and off by default.

faq.q: Can I switch modes after I pass?
faq.a: Yes. Drivest supports Learner, New Driver, and Standard modes.
UK first. EU expansion is planned next, then North America. Timing depends on localisation and validation.

sections.title: AI voice coach
sections.text: A guided voice layer that sequences prompts like a driving instructor. Designed to stay short and non-intrusive.

sections.title: Smarter risk tuning
sections.text: More context-aware prompts with stricter confidence rules and improved stress scoring.

sections.title: More regions
sections.text: UK first. EU planned next, then North America. Each region requires local road rule tuning and pack validation.

sections.title: In-car support
sections.text: Android Auto and Apple CarPlay support is a post-launch goal.
